profile.feeling: Eyes open, the first light — the moment sleep ends.

examples.text: 我今天早上六点就醒了。
examples.py: Wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang liù diǎn jiù xǐng le.
examples.tr: I was awake by six this morning.
Is the child awake (yet)?
He is still awake.

collocations.tr: to wake up, to come round

synonyms.nuance: xǐnglái: wake up, come to — often in narration: 他醒来的时候…
qǐchuáng: get up, get out of bed — 醒 is only opening your eyes

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 酉 ‘alcohol’ + phonetic 星; Wiktionary lists ‘to sober up; to regain consciousness’ and ‘to wake up’ among its senses, and relates it to 清 ‘clear’ (Schuessler 2007).

funFacts: 醒 is also ‘to sober up’ (醒酒) — which is why its left part is 酉, the ‘wine jar’ component.
pitfalls: 醒 is only waking up; getting out of bed is 起床: 我六点醒了，七点才起床 ‘I woke at six but didn’t get up till seven’.
To wake SOMEONE ELSE is 叫醒 ‘call awake’: 妈妈七点叫醒我 — not *妈妈醒我.
subtleties: 醒了 = has woken, is awake now (the 了 of a new situation); 醒着 = is (lying) awake, a lasting state (C02).

tradPerSense.none: written the same in traditional characters

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

separable.none: a single verb, nothing goes inside

profile.feeling: The alarm rings, the blanket is thrown back — the start of the day.

senses.def: to get up, to get out of bed

examples.tr: I get up at seven every day.
Get up, quick! We’re going to be late!

examples.py: Xīngqītiān wǒ hěn wǎn cái qǐchuáng.
examples.tr: On Sundays I don’t get up till late.

collocations.tr: to get up in the morning

phrases.tr: early to bed, early to rise — good for the body
phrases.meaning: go to bed early and get up early to stay healthy

synonyms.nuance: qǐlái: get up (from bed or from a seat) — 快起来！
qǐ: get up — short, in set phrases: 早睡早起
qǐshēn: rise, get up

etymology.text: 起 ‘to rise’ + 床 ‘bed’: a verb–object word, ‘rise from the bed’; Wiktionary writes it 起⫽床 (separable).

funFacts: The saying 早睡早起身体好 ‘early to bed, early to rise keeps you healthy’ uses the short 起 for 起床.
pitfalls: 起床 already has its object (床): nothing else can follow it; 了 may go inside it in narration (起了床就走).
subtleties: 起床 is getting out of bed, 醒 is waking up: you can 醒 at six and 起床 at seven.

tradPerSense.none: written the same in traditional characters

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

profile.feeling: Water, soap and clean hands — washing anything at all.

senses.def: to wash (oneself, a part of the body, clothes, dishes)

examples.tr: Wash your hands before eating.

examples.py: Zǎoshang wǒ yòng lěngshuǐ xǐ liǎn.
examples.tr: In the morning I wash my face in cold water.
Mum is doing the washing.

phrases.tr: wash one’s ears and listen respectfully

synonyms.nuance: chōng: rinse (under running water)
shuā: brush, scrub — 刷牙 ‘brush one’s teeth’

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 水 ‘water’ + phonetic 先. From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *sjərl ‘to wash; to bathe’; cognate with Tibetan བསིལ (bsil) ‘to wash’ (Schuessler 2007, STEDT).

funFacts: 洗手间 ‘wash-hands room’ is the polite word for the toilet (S12).
pitfalls: Teeth are brushed, not washed: 刷牙; 洗牙 is a cleaning at the dentist’s.
洗 also develops photos (洗照片), shuffles cards (洗牌) and launders money (洗钱) — the object decides.
subtleties: 洗 needs what is washed: 洗手, 洗脸, 洗衣服; washing all over is 洗澡.

tradPerSense.none: written the same in traditional characters

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

separable.none: a single verb that takes an object (洗手, 洗衣服)

profile.feeling: Hot water after a long day — shower or bath, it is all 洗澡.

senses.def: to take a shower or a bath, to wash oneself

examples.tr: I shower every evening.

examples.text: 他正在洗澡，不能接电话。
examples.py: Tā zhèngzài xǐzǎo, bù néng jiē diànhuà.
examples.tr: He’s in the shower and can’t take the call.
After getting up I shower first.

collocations.tr: to have a quick wash, a shower
to have a hot shower or bath

synonyms.nuance: chōngzǎo: take a shower (rinsing under running water)
pàozǎo: soak in a bath
mùyù: bathe

etymology.text: 洗 ‘to wash’ + 澡 ‘to wash the body’ (澡 is no longer used alone): a verb–object word, Wiktionary 洗⫽澡.

funFacts: Chinese makes no difference between a shower and a bath: both are 洗澡. The shower itself is 淋浴 (línyù), the bathtub 浴缸 (yùgǎng).
pitfalls: 洗澡 already has its object: *洗澡身体 is wrong. 了 and 个 go inside: 洗了个澡.
subtleties: 洗了个澡 with 个 sounds light and quick — ‘had a quick wash’.

tradPerSense.none: written the same in traditional characters

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

override.meaning: Wiktionary glosses 穿衣 ‘to put on clothes; to dress; to wear clothes’ — the same meaning as the concept ‘to get dressed’, in other words.

profile.feeling: Shirt, trousers, socks — getting ready to face the day.

senses.def: to get dressed, to put on one’s clothes

examples.text: 孩子已经会自己穿衣了。
examples.py: Háizi yǐjīng huì zìjǐ chuānyī le.
examples.tr: The child can already dress himself.

examples.text: 我起床、洗脸、穿衣，然后吃早饭。
examples.py: Wǒ qǐchuáng, xǐ liǎn, chuānyī, ránhòu chī zǎofàn.
examples.tr: I get up, wash my face, get dressed and then have breakfast.

examples.py: Tiān lěng le, yào duō chuānyī.
examples.tr: It’s getting cold — wrap up warm.

collocations.tr: to put on clothes (the full spoken form)

synonyms.nuance: chuān yīfu: the usual spoken form, with the full noun 衣服 ‘clothes’ (C08)
chuānshang: put on + the garment (穿上外套)
dǎban: dress up, make oneself look nice

etymology.text: 穿 ‘to pass through; to put on, to wear’ + 衣 ‘clothes’: ‘put on clothes’. Wiktionary writes it 穿⫽衣 (separable) and glosses it ‘to put on clothes; to dress’.

funFacts: 穿 first meant ‘to bore through, to pierce’ — you pass through a sleeve or a shoe: 穿衣, 穿鞋.
pitfalls: In speech ‘get dressed’ is usually 穿衣服, with the full noun 衣服; 穿衣 is the short form of lists and advice (起床穿衣, 多穿衣).
Hats, glasses and watches are not 穿 but 戴 (C08).
subtleties: 穿 covers both putting on and wearing (C08): 他在穿衣 ‘he is getting dressed’, 他穿着红衣服 ‘he is wearing red’.

tradPerSense.none: written the same in traditional characters

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

profile.feeling: Keys, phone, door shut behind you — out into the street.

senses.def: to go out, to leave the house
to be away from home, to set off on a journey

examples.py: Wǒ bā diǎn chūmén qù shàngbān.
examples.tr: I leave home at eight to go to work.

examples.py: Wàimiàn xià yǔ, bié chūmén le.
examples.tr: It’s raining outside — don’t go out.
He has gone away travelling.

collocations.tr: as soon as one steps out
to go on a long journey

phrases.text: 在家千日好，出门一时难
phrases.tr: at home a thousand days are fine, away from home one hour is hard
phrases.meaning: travelling is hard; nothing beats home

synonyms.nuance: chūqù: go out (away from here) — the direction, not leaving home
líkāi jiā: leave home — also for good

etymology.text: 出 ‘to go out’ + 门 ‘door, gate’: ‘go out of the door’; Wiktionary writes it 出⫽門 (separable).

funFacts: Wiktionary also records older senses: a woman marrying out of her family, and a funeral procession leaving the house.
pitfalls: 出门 is going out, not leaving for good: 他出门了 ‘he has gone out’; moving out of home is 离开家 / 搬出去.
subtleties: 一出门就… ‘as soon as I stepped out …’: 我一出门就下雨了.

tradPerSense.none: traditional 出門 for every sense

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

contrasts.value: the general verb: begin (+ verb or noun) — 开始工作, 电影开始了

profile.feeling: The whistle blows, the lights go down — something gets going.

senses.def: to start, to begin (+ verb or noun); to start (of an event)
(noun) the beginning: 开始的时候, 一开始

examples.tr: We start work at nine.
The film has started!

examples.text: 开始的时候，我觉得中文很难。
examples.py: Kāishǐ de shíhou, wǒ juéde Zhōngwén hěn nán.
examples.tr: At the beginning I found Chinese hard.

synonyms.nuance: kāi: start — only in set words: 开会, 开学
kāitóu: begin; the beginning
qǐ: 从…起 ‘starting from …’

etymology.text: 开 ‘to open’ + 始 ‘beginning’ (as in 始终 ‘from beginning to end’).

funFacts: 从今天开始 ‘starting today’: 从 … 开始 frames a starting point, as 从 … 到 … frames a stretch (S15).
pitfalls: 开始 + verb needs no word for ‘to’: 开始学中文 ‘start learning Chinese’.
subtleties: 开始了 = has begun, is under way now; 开始的时候 / 一开始 = at the beginning, at first.

tradPerSense.none: traditional 開始 for every sense

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

separable.none: not a verb–object word: nothing goes inside

contrasts.value: an event or an activity ends, or someone ends it (会议结束了, 结束工作)

profile.feeling: The last bell, the closing credits — it is over.

senses.def: to end, to finish, to come to an end; to bring to an end

examples.tr: What time does the meeting end?

examples.text: 假期结束了，我们回家吧。
examples.py: Jiàqī jiéshù le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.
examples.tr: The holiday is over — let’s go home.

examples.text: 他七点结束工作，然后回家。
examples.py: Tā qī diǎn jiéshù gōngzuò, ránhòu huí jiā.
examples.tr: He finishes work at seven and then goes home.

synonyms.nuance: wán: finish, be over — after a verb (吃完 ‘eat up’) or alone (电影完了)
wánchéng: complete, accomplish (a task)
tíngzhǐ: stop (something still going)

etymology.text: 结 ‘to tie, to knot’ + 束 ‘to bind’. Wiktionary also records the archaic senses ‘to dress up’ and ‘to pack up for a journey’.

funFacts: The opposite pair 开始 / 结束 frames every event: 会议九点开始，十点结束.
pitfalls: 结束 is ‘come to an end’, not ‘use up’: *咖啡结束了 → 咖啡喝完了 / 没有了.
subtleties: 结束 ends things that go on (a meeting, a war, a holiday); finishing a piece of work is usually verb + 完: 做完, 吃完 (C33).

tradPerSense.none: traditional 結束 for every sense

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

separable.none: not a verb–object word: nothing goes inside

contrasts.value: the plain activity, often alone (我要睡觉了)

profile.feeling: Lights out, pillow, blanket — bedtime and the night’s sleep.

examples.tr: What time do you go to bed?

examples.py: Shíyī diǎn le, gāi shuìjiào le.
examples.tr: It’s eleven — time for bed.
The child is asleep — don’t talk.
I didn’t sleep last night.

synonyms.nuance: shuì: sleep — with a length or a result after it (睡八个小时, 睡着)
xiūxi: rest — also a polite ‘go to bed’ (你早点休息吧)
jiùqǐn: retire for the night

etymology.text: 睡 ‘to sleep’ + 觉 jiào ‘a sleep’: a verb–object word, Wiktionary 睡⫽覺.

funFacts: 觉 has two readings: jiào ‘a sleep’ (睡觉, 午觉) and jué ‘to feel, to become aware’ (觉得). Wiktionary even records an old 睡觉 read shuìjué ‘to wake up’.
pitfalls: 睡觉 already has its object, so a length goes with 睡: 睡了八个小时 (or split: 睡了八个小时的觉), not *睡觉了八个小时.
跟…睡觉 can mean ‘to sleep with someone’ — context decides.
subtleties: 睡觉 is both ‘go to bed’ and ‘sleep’: 我十一点睡觉 ‘I go to bed at eleven’, 他在睡觉 ‘he is asleep’.

readings.none: one reading in every sense: shuìjiào (觉 is jiào in this word)

tradPerSense.none: traditional 睡覺 for every sense

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

contrasts.value: with what follows: a length, a result, a place (睡八个小时, 睡着, 睡在床上)

profile.feeling: Deep, light, long or short — sleep itself.

examples.py: Wǒ zuótiān shuìle bā ge xiǎoshí.
examples.tr: I slept eight hours last night.
Did you sleep well?
He sleeps on the sofa.

collocations.tr: to sleep in, to have a lie-in
early to bed, early to rise

synonyms.nuance: shuìjiào: the activity — go to bed, sleep
shuìmián: sleep (the noun: 睡眠不好 ‘poor sleep’)
mián: sleep (in compounds: 失眠 ‘insomnia’)

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 目 ‘eye’ + phonetic 垂; Wiktionary (after STEDT) suggests a link with 垂 ‘to hang down’.

funFacts: A memory aid: the eye 目 next to 垂 ‘hanging down’ — drooping eyelids.
pitfalls: The length comes after 睡: 睡了八个小时; 睡觉 cannot take it (*睡觉八个小时).
subtleties: 睡 is the verb that takes complements: 睡着 ‘fall asleep’, 睡不着 ‘can’t sleep’, 睡得好 ‘sleep well’.

tradPerSense.none: written the same in traditional characters

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

separable.none: a single verb; results and lengths follow it (睡着, 睡八个小时)

profile.feeling: Drifting off — the moment you are finally gone.

senses.def: to fall asleep, to get to sleep

examples.tr: I didn’t fall asleep until twelve.
I couldn’t get to sleep last night.
The child has fallen asleep.

synonyms.nuance: rùshuì: fall asleep (in writing, medicine)
chéngmián: fall asleep — mostly in 难以成眠 ‘unable to sleep’

etymology.text: 睡 ‘to sleep’ + 着 zháo ‘to reach, to succeed’: a verb with its result, ‘sleep and get there’ (Wiktionary: verb-complement 睡⫽著).

funFacts: 着 here is zháo, as in 找着 ‘search and find’ — the result reached — not the toneless zhe of a lasting state (C02).
pitfalls: 睡着 shuìzháo ‘fall asleep’ and 睡着 shuìzhe ‘sleeping (in a lasting state)’ are written alike; 睡着了 with 了 is nearly always zháo.
subtleties: Not falling asleep is 没睡着 (didn’t manage) or 睡不着 (can’t) — never *不睡着.

readings.none: one reading: shuìzháo (着 is zháo in this word)

tradPerSense.none: traditional 睡著 for every sense

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

separable.none: a verb with its result (睡 + 着): 得 / 不 can go between (睡得着, 睡不着), but no object

lexemes.role: already — 已经 … 了 with a completed action or a point reached (他已经起床了, 已经十点了) (C01); ‘already’ in depth comes with aspect (C40)

contrasts.value: 已经 + verb (+ 了): already — the plain everyday word (他已经走了)

profile.feeling: Done before you asked — the matter is already behind us.

senses.def: already (with 了: an action done, a point reached)

examples.tr: He’s already up.
I’ve already had breakfast.

examples.py: Yǐjīng shí diǎn le, kuài zǒu ba!
examples.tr: It’s already ten — let’s go!

synonyms.nuance: zǎojiù: long ago, long since (我早就知道了)
yǐ: already — in writing (已到 ‘has arrived’)
dōu: 都…了 ‘already!’, with surprise (都十点了)

etymology.text: 已 ‘to stop; already’ + 经 ‘to pass through’ (as in 经过): ‘already passed’.

funFacts: 已 yǐ ‘already’, 己 jǐ ‘self’ and 巳 sì (an Earthly Branch) differ only in how far one stroke closes.
pitfalls: 已经 almost always goes with 了: 他已经走了 — *他已经走 sounds unfinished.
Its negative is not *已经没 but 还没 (hái méi) ‘not yet’: 他还没起床.
subtleties: 已经 + a time or a number + 了 needs no verb: 已经十点了 ‘it’s already ten’, 他已经二十岁了 ‘he’s already twenty’.

tradPerSense.none: traditional 已經 for every sense

toneSandhi.none: no 一 or 不 in the word

absent.reason: No verb for having breakfast: Chinese says ‘eat breakfast’ with the verb 吃 (S07) and the noun 早饭 (S07).
absent.use: 吃早饭 (written also 吃早餐): 我七点吃早饭 ‘I have breakfast at seven’; 你吃早饭了吗？ ‘have you had breakfast?’; done: 我吃了早饭就出门 / 我已经吃早饭了.

absent.reason: No word of its own in the course: ‘come home’ is 回 ‘to return’ (S13) + 家 ‘home’ (S06), said as one unit (huí jiā). Dictionaries list 回家 as a word; the course keeps the two words it has taught, as in every earlier sentence.
absent.use: 回家: 我六点回家 ‘I come home at six’; 他回家了 ‘he has gone / come home’; 回到家 ‘to get home’; towards the speaker 回家来 / 回来.
